deprecated_yaml.title: The MeteoSwiss YAML configuration is being removed
deprecated_yaml.description:
Configuring MeteoSwiss using YAML is being removed.

Your existing YAML configuration has been imported into the UI automatically.

Remove the MeteoSwiss configuration from your configuration.yaml file and restart Home Assistant to fix this issue.

station_no_data.title: MeteoSwiss weather station appears to be gone
station_no_data.description:
The real-time weather station MeteoSwiss is using ({station}) is no longer offering data.

Currently, the only repair possible involves removing and re-adding the MeteoSwiss integration, selecting a new real-time weather station.

Until this repair is made, all real-time weather sensors and reports coming from this station will show as unavailable.

postcode_no_data.title: MeteoSwiss appears not to provide forecasts for postal code
postcode_no_data.description:
The postal code {postcode} does not appear to have any forecast available.

Currently, the only repair possible involves removing and re-adding the MeteoSwiss integration, selecting a new post code.

Until this repair is made, the forecast will show as unavailable.

improperly_configured.title: MeteoSwiss integration improperly configured
improperly_configured.description:
The MeteoSwiss integration with entry ID {entry_id} is improperly configured.

Please remove your configuration entry and recreate it.

point_no_data.title: MeteoSwiss no longer provides a forecast for a place
point_no_data.description:
MeteoSwiss does not appear to offer a forecast for {name} any more.

Remove and re-add the MeteoSwiss integration for this place, choosing another one.

Until then, its forecast will show as unavailable.

user.description: Confirm your geographical position.  This will be used to guess the closest real-time weather station and approximate your postal code for forecasts.
user.title: Location

location.title: Forecast for
location.description: Use the forecast of a postal code, or of a mountain, hut or pass.

user_two.description: The postal code is used to look up the nine-day forecast.  The name you enter here will be used for the forecast (weather) entity.
user_two.title: Forecast

data_description.hourly_temperature: MeteoSwiss only publishes hourly temperatures in one file for all of Switzerland, so they cost a 33 MB download every three hours (about 260 MB a day, 8 GB a month), shared by all your MeteoSwiss forecasts. Mountain forecasts also download the freezing level, another file of the same size. Turn this off on a metered connection: the hourly forecast then has no temperatures, and the rest of the forecast needs only a few kilobytes an hour.

mountain.title: Mountain, hut or pass
mountain.description: Places are sorted by distance from your location, and their forecasts are for the altitude shown.  Only the 100 closest are listed.  Without a station, the current conditions shown are the forecast for the current hour.

data_description.forecast_name: Leave empty to use the name of the place.
data_description.hourly_temperature: MeteoSwiss only publishes hourly temperatures and the freezing level in files for all of Switzerland, of about 33 MB each, downloaded every three hours (about 530 MB a day, 16 GB a month, shared with your other MeteoSwiss forecasts). Turn this off on a metered connection: the forecast then has no hourly temperatures and there is no freezing level sensor.

user_three.description:
The real-time weather and precipitation stations are used to look up the current weather and precipitation at the station and provide them as sensors.  Selecting the first option of the list disables real-time weather sensors.

If a weather station is selected, the real-time entity names field is used to name the real-time (sensor) entities.  If no station is chosen, the real-time entity names field is ignored.

{station_url} lists the available real-time stations.
user_three.title: Real-time weather and precipitation stations

Mountain forecasts also download the freezing level, another file of the same size. Turn this off on a metered connection: the hourly forecast then has no temperatures, and the rest of the forecast needs only a few kilobytes an hour.
